entities.name: Paulo da Gama
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Paulo da Gama was a Portuguese explorer, son of Estêvão da Gama and Isabel Sodré, and the older brother of Vasco da Gama.

Born in the Kingdom of Portugal around 1450, Paulo da Gama embarked on several expeditions under the patronage of King Manuel I of Portugal.

In 1491, Paulo da Gama led an expedition to West Africa, becoming the first European to reach the Cape Verde islands.

This voyage marked the beginning of Portuguese exploration and trade in the Atlantic, establishing connections with the Kingdom of Kongo and the Sultanate of Kilwa.

Paulo da Gama's journey also laid the groundwork for Vasco da Gama's famous voyage around Africa in 1497-1499, which would change the course of world history.

Despite his significant contributions to Portuguese exploration, Paulo da Gama's life remains somewhat overshadowed by his more famous brother.

However, his legacy as a pioneering explorer and navigator continues to inspire historians and scholars today.

As Vasco da Gama once said, 'The sea is the greatest of all masters.' Paulo da Gama embodied this spirit of adventure and discovery, leaving an indelible mark on the history of exploration and beyond.
